minutes.summary: After an executive session on collective bargaining, the board heard comments on the new town manager selection and a cemetery records complaint. The board also discussed the Community Preservation Act, tax title foreclosure rules and the interim town manager's report, and approved minutes as amended.

what_happened.line: The Select Board spent most of the meeting workshopping a draft employee climate survey policy and did not adopt it.
By consensus the board moved the survey timeline so results arrive about November 1 and set the survey to run every two years instead of annually.
The board kept the final choice of survey vendor and questions for itself and again asked for the full engagement survey results and the vendor's draft questions.
The board took no decision on retaining the tax title property at 55 Carver Avenue.
The interim town manager said the retirement assessment rose by about half of the expected new town-side revenue, and the board approved minutes as amended.

why_it_matters: A survey every two years run by an outside vendor would add a recurring consultant cost to the town-side budget, and the board wanted the timing set sooner than a split across two fiscal years would allow.
The retirement assessment taking up about half of expected new town-side revenue leaves less room for other town services under the levy limit.
The 55 Carver Avenue property and the Community Preservation Act steps both remain open, and a CPA surcharge would be a vote residents are asked to take.
watch_next: The survey policy returning to the board for adoption, with the full engagement survey results and the vendor's draft questions the board requested.
A board decision on whether to retain 55 Carver Avenue through the tax title process.
